notes: Dev RBox revision. Flips a property that holds: corresponding is exchanging letters, so 'corresponded with' is symmetric (staging/literature_arts.RELATIONS.md); the edit makes it asymmetric, the same shape as the other topics' dev RBox revisions and the geography template (twinned_with). It replaces the earlier adapted_from edit (review 2026-11-11): that edit started from asymmetry, which the dataset no longer uses, and its instances (The Wizard of Oz, Jaws) had a second route to the old answers through stored dates, since a novel cannot be adapted from a later film. The instances use made-up writers and artists given in the prompt, so no stored fact about them competes with the property; the question asks what follows. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question asks 'asymmetric' (no, then yes), the first instance whether the converse follows (yes, then no), the second whether the converse is ruled out (no, then yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance, the Chinese one as a 是否 question so 是/否 are the natural answers. Near unrelated asks the same property of a neighbouring symmetric literature relation (co-wrote a book with: not asymmetric), which an edit that spreads asymmetry to related relations would flip; far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. collaborated_with was avoided because the main split edits it (literature 0010); corresponded_with is new. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge, as the template does. The four people in the instances are made up: Wikipedia searches for "Marta Velling", "Oskar Brandvik", "Ines Carrow" and "Lukas Ferrand" each had 0 hits on 2026-11-11. The instance sentences are stated in their prompts, so they carry no evidence entry (only an inserted fact may be claimed fictional) and need no check. Review 2026-11-12: the direct question was reworded from "Is the relation 'corresponded with' asymmetric?" (two models answered yes to the term) to the plain-language meaning of asymmetry. Round 3 (2026-11-13): direct reworded to the same concrete frame as its paired contraction delete-d003.
